They haven’t kissed since that night in the library. The thing between them grew too fast and too fragile for there to be any way to talk about it. And when they woke up the next morning, face to face, in the same bed they always sleep in, something felt so inexplicably different that Phainon had panicked and brushed off the need to discuss any potential changes to their relationship. He chalked it up to the late night and the magic of the library. What relationship they did have was still so new, and it was good; Phainon couldn’t bear it if that got taken away from him too. Mydei didn’t seem keen to mention it or initiate anything more, so Phainon assumed he felt the same.

However, it would be a lie to say that nothing has changed since the kiss.

“Remind me how this all goes?” Phainon asks, propped up on his elbow, looking down at Mydei, who still lies sprawled on their bed, one leg hooked over Phainon’s.

Mydei grumbles. They’ve been over this before. “My birthday is tomorrow, and with it my coming of age ceremony. Since I’m the crown prince there’s a whole traditional party and a bunch of ceremonies starting today,” he says flatly.

“And the tattooing,” Phainon adds.

“And the tattooing,” Mydei says with a nod. “But that one comes last.”

“And you aren’t looking forward to this because?”

Mydei groans and finally opens his eyes to properly look at Phainon. “Because it’s a waste of resources. It is foolish to throw such a big party when we’ve only just reclaimed our land from the Black Tide. And I’ve never liked these celebrations. It’s too much attention.”

“See, that doesn’t sound like you,” Phainon says, poking Mydei’s cheek. “I’ve seen you command whole legions, I’ve seen you give speeches. You aren’t scared are you?” he teases.

“I am not scared,” Mydei hisses, untangling their legs to kick Phainon in the shin.

Phainon yelps and kicks Mydei back, but he’s smiling. They’re both smiling. It’s been nice, over the past few weeks, to spend their mornings chatting away idly, instead of pretending they don’t share a bed.

The fluttering light surges in Phainon’s chest, slipping through his defenses. It never stays still for long these days. “I don’t think celebration is a waste of resources,” he says, unable to stop himself from saying something painfully earnest. “Especially when it’s celebrating you.”

Mydei blushes, his face and chest going red. It makes Phainon feel giddy, a little light-headed. Ever since discovering how easily Mydei blushes, and how cute he is when flustered, Phaion has made it his mission to get a rise out of Mydei as often as he can–often to his own detriment. Whether it’s goading Mydei into a pointless competition, or admitting something he should probably keep hidden, Phainon can’t help himself when it comes to Mydei.

Mydei frowns, harsh expression completely undercut by his blush, and Phainon has to bite back a laugh.

“You say such outrageous things,” Mydei grumbles.

“You wound me!” Phainon gasps. He opens his mouth to say more, to continue the act, when at that exact moment, the door to their room swings open with no warning, and the somatophylakes burst into the room in a loud gaggle of overlapping voices.

“Today is the day!”

“Time to party!”

“Avert your eyes! The happy couple is in bed!”

The clamor fills the room as boys stumble in and swarm the bed, beaming down at the two of them.

Phainon and Mydei flinch apart on instinct. It’s a foolish attempt. They’ve clearly been caught,

and it is a bit ridiculous to be so embarrassed to be seen acting as a married couple should. But Phainon thinks it’s only reasonable to want some privacy in these moments of growing intimacy.

They both protest the intrusion. Phainon yelps as he scrambles away from Mydei, pulling the blanket up to cover his chest, like he’s been caught in a lewd act. Mydei moves away from Phainon just as fast, yelling pointlessly for his friends to get out. He doesn’t bother covering up, but considering how red he still is, maybe he should abandon the Kremnos’ relaxed view on modesty.

“Aw, are you embarrassed?" Perdikkas teases.

“No,” Mydei says, lying.

“Are you going to tell us that Kremnoans never get embarrassed?" Ptolemy adds.

“I don’t,” Mydei retorts, pulling a laugh from all of them, even Phainon.

“I think it’s cute,” Hephaestion says, smiling wide.

Mydei grumbles, but stops protesting. It’s sweet, Phainon thinks, seeing how freely they interact. Years of friendship and inside jokes have shaped the way they tease and play. It always amazes Phainon that Mydei and his friends found a way to carve out a space of boyish levity that’s lasted as long as it has. No one their age, Okheman, Kremnoan or otherwise, has been spared the pain and hardship of the Black Tide, but Mydei and his friends have made a valiant effort to retain some part of their youth.

“Sorry if this is a dumb question, but why are you all here?” Phainon asks. Even with the somatophylakes’ contagious excitement, Phainon mourns the loss of his quiet morning with Mydei.

“Celebration starts early, my friend!” Perdikkas says, hands on his hips as if he’s making an important proclamation.

“Mydei told you his birthday festivities start today, right?” Leonnius asks.

“He did,” Phainon says, still unsure how this answers his question.

“It’s our own tradition,” Mydei says, seeming to shed some of his earlier tension. “It’s been a running joke for years. Whenever it’s one of our birthdays, the rest of us try to start the celebration via ambush. But this does seem excessively early.”

“Well, we wanted to include Phainon as well,” Hephaestion says, waving off Mydei’s concern. “And this is the only time we knew for sure you two would be in the same place.”

“And we thought it would be funny,” Perdikkas says.

“It is pretty funny,” Ptolemy agrees with a laugh. “I don’t think I’ve ever seen Mydei blush like this, and Phainon’s acting like we caught you two fucking.”

“Hey,” Mydei exclaims.

“We were not!” Phainon protests at the same time.

“I dunno, kinda sounds like you two were fuckin’,” Hephaestion says with a crooked grin. It’s an unusually crass remark from him, and all the boys erupt in excited jeers.

Phainon laughs, despite himself, mouth and eyes wide in shock.

For Mydei, this seems to be a step too far. His expression flashes from shock to anger in an instant as Hephaestion’s words register.

“Alright, that’s enough!” Mydei exclaims. He jumps out of bed and starts pushing his friends out of the room. Everyone erupts into a cacophony of laughter and yelling. Phainon considers helping Mydei–it does seem unfair to have him go five against one–but ultimately Phainon lets Mydei take the fight. It doesn’t feel like it’s quite his place, and in the end, Mydei doesn’t need the help.

Once the somatophylakes are gone, Mydei returns to Phainon’s side. “Sorry about them,” he says, falling back onto the bed with a heavy sigh. The bed sinks with his weight and Phainon allows himself to slide closer to Mydei, seeking out his warmth.

“I think they’re nice,” Phainon says with a laugh.

Mydei squints at Phainon, a small furrow between his eyebrows. It takes all Phainon has not to reach over and smooth out the crease between them.

“They’ve gotten you on their side,” Mydei laments.

“What can I say,” Phainon says with a grin. “Maybe they have charmed their way into my good graces.” He wriggles his toes, now cold, against Mydei’s leg to add to his teasing.

Mydei gasps and scrambles out of bed. “HKS!” he exclaims, looking at Phainon with betrayal.

“Oh, you’ve done worse,” Phainon retorts. When Mydei crosses his arms and maintains his irritated facade, Phainon relents. “What? So that was the last straw and now it’s time to get up?”

“Yes,” Mydei says simply. Phainon suspects he would also prefer to stay in bed longer but has now backed himself into a corner.

“Fine,” Phainon whines. He’s not actually that upset at starting the day. In all honesty, he’s excited to see what the birthday festivities bring, but he will miss their private cocoon of softness. It is hard to be so gentle and affectionate when other people are around. It makes them all too aware of who they are supposed to be, and how much work they all still have to do fighting the Black Tide.

Phainon slips out of bed and pads over to Mydei, before nudging him softly, wordlessly asking to braid his hair. Mydei tilts his head automatically, giving Phainon better access. Phainon’s gotten quite good at braiding Mydei’s hair at this point, and the act has become a comfortable morning ritual for the two of them. This particular morning, Phainon feels like his heart is going to jump out of his chest and he’s convinced Mydei will be able to feel his heartbeat in his fingertips. Mydei’s hair is soft and his skin is warm; and Phainon’s heart aches. The small patch of delicate skin under Mydei’s ear, exposed by the braid, all but begs for a kiss. Only at the last minute does Phainon stop himself from bending forward and listening to the call.

“All done,” Phainon says, slapping Mydei on the shoulders, his voice higher than usual. He takes a somewhat frantic step back from Mydei, desperate to put some distance between them. Every second spent so close to Mydei, Phainon feels as if he might be torn into pieces. His desire wars with his common sense and the small–but ever louder–voice asking why shouldn’t he court Mydei.

“You’ve gotten good at this,” Mydei says, inspecting the braid. The compliment goes right to Phainon’s head and he smiles wide, crinkling his eyes and showing his teeth.

“Thank you,” Phainon says, chipper. They stare at each other for a beat, Phainon bouncing slightly on the balls of his feet as they do. Braiding Mydei’s hair is the unofficial end of their cozy mornings, yet neither of them seem ready to move.

“So, what’s next?” Phainon asks when staring into Mydei’s eyes gets to be too much for his fragile heart.

“Well, first I have to spend around two hours in the temple with my parents,” Mydei says, trying to hide a groan. “Then I will receive jewelry from my mother and wine from my father. Then we all sit while a group of citizens presents a gift to the family. And that’s all before lunch.” Mydei continues listing off rituals and celebrations until he reaches the evening, at which the two of them will have some time together before the main party in the evening.

“Wow, they really are making you work for this,” Phainon says, mildly disappointed. Many of the events in the morning are for blood relatives only, so Phainon will have to occupy himself until later.

“They are,” Mydei agrees grumpily. Then he closes his eyes and takes a long breath, chasing away his complaints. “It’s fine. It’s nothing I haven’t done before in one way or another. Some of it will even be fun.”

“Alright, if you say so,” Phainon says, fully aware that Mydei has to go through this whether he wants to or not.

“I do wish you could join me,” Mydei blurts out.

Phainon’s heart clenches, his chest seemingly trying to collapse in on itself in utter delight. Mydei does not hide his feelings the way Phainon does. He wears his heart on his sleeve and takes great care to only share his thoughts once he is certain how he feels. So this impulsive admission is rare, and Phainon will cherish every kind word and whispered confession he gets. He has amassed quite the collection of half-heard sweetness, but it’s not enough to convince him to listen to the light in his chest. That will wait until Mydei says something direct, undeniable. It’s been made very clear that Mydei does not give hints or say half-truths in hope that Phainon will pick up on them. So, for now, Phainon will continue to collect these rare treasures and wait until Mydei is ready.

Phainon has to cough before he can speak, his throat too tight with emotion. “That would be nice,” he agrees once his voice is working again.

Mydei nods once, unusually rigid, his jaw working like he’s thinking through something complex. It seems like he might have more to say, something else to add on to his earlier admission. Phainon waits for Mydei to figure out his words, trying to hide just the way he’s buzzing with energy under his skin.

After long seconds of thinking, Mydei sighs, deflating a little. “Alright, I’ll see you later, then,” Mydei says flatly, ending the conversation before it truly begins.

“Yeah, see you later,” Phainon replies softly. Then Mydei gathers his things and is on his way, leaving Phainon alone with his thoughts and the uphill battle of composing himself before the evening.

***

The day passes strangely for Phainon. He putts about reading and wasting time. He asks if he can assist with preparations, but no one takes him up on his offers. Despite the lack of anything to do and Phainon’s overactive thoughts, the time still passes quickly, as if the festive atmosphere has given the whole day an extra shine to it to bolster it along.

This strange atmosphere persists even when Mydei returns from his celebratory duties. It isn’t a bad strangeness, but the world still feels a little too quick and a little too bright as the two of them get ready for the evening. Mydei bathes, redresses in proper formal attire, and then spends far too long fussing over Phainon’s new Kremnoan outfit. Phainon isn’t sure how long this actually takes, he’s too busy trying not to combust every time Mydei’s fingers graze his bare skin to pay attention to something as trivial as time.

It all comes to a head when they are just about to leave and Mydei stops Phainon on his way out, grabbing him by the wrist and dragging him back to the large mirror in their room.

“Stay still,” Mydei orders, and despite his instinct to do the opposite of whatever Mydei says, Phainon freezes, too focused on the lingering warmth of Mydei’s hand to tease.

Mydei dips out of view for a moment and returns with a small brush and a bowl of gold paint.

“I mean it,” he says, voice serious but refusing to look Phainon in the eyes, “don’t move.”

“Okay,” Phainon whispers.

Mydei grabs his chin. All five fingers press into his skin so searingly hot that Phainon will be shocked if they don’t leave burns behind. If Phainon thought he had been still before, it’s nothing compared to how tense he stands now, hardly daring to breathe.

With no further explanation, Mydei dips the brush into the golden paint and brings it to Phainon’s face. The paint is brutally cold in comparison to Mydei’s hand– Phainon is astonished he didn’t twitch when it first touched his skin. Locked in the painful tug of hot and cold, Phainon waits, almost faint, as Mydei paints a small shape below his right eye.

Mydei pulls away after an incalculable amount of time. Seconds? Years? Phainon suspects he will never know.

“There, finished,” Mydei announces, still without any explanation, like that makes any sense. “Now hurry up, or we’ll be late.” He turns on his heel, the long cape of his formal wear flaring out dramatically behind him, and walks out of the room without waiting for Phainon, the rhythmic click of his footsteps growing quieter the longer Phainon stares after him in shock.

Only when the door swings shut, cutting off Mydei from view, does Phainon finally return to himself with the feeling of suddenly snapping back into the correct flow of time. He shivers slightly, somehow cold in Mydei’s absence, before turning to the mirror, leaning closer to inspect what Mydei painted on his face.

Below his eye, a familiar shape greets him in the mirror. Except this time, the ink is gold instead of red, and the flame-like diamond sits on his face instead of Mydei’s

Mydei made the two of them match.

Phainon’s heart squeezes so tightly he thinks he might faint. Or explode. Or somehow else be consumed by the massiveness of his emotions. He wants to stare in the mirror until Mydei’s claim on him is imprinted into his memory like a brand–he wants to study it like a sacred artifact. He wants to twirl around the room and kick his feet like a child with a schoolyard crush. He wants to run after Mydei and kiss him stupid for the rest of the night, birthday party be damned. Phainon thinks he wants just about everything so long as it involves Mydei.

The door bangs back open and Phainon jumps, scuttling away from the mirror as Mydei barges back into the room.

“Phainon!” Mydei exclaims, exasperated, almost fully angry. “We can’t actually be late!”

“Sorry! Sorry!” Phainon says, scrambling to get up, smoothing out his chiton as he hurries to the door. “Okay, let’s go,” he says, tossing Mydei a wide but lopsided smile in hopes of diffusing some of the anger. Mydei huffs and rolls his eyes but doesn’t scold him anymore. Phainon takes this as a win.

This time Mydei doesn’t give Phainon a chance to get left behind, grabbing him by the wrist and dragging him painfully out of the room toward the party.

***

The grand hall has been completely transformed for the event. All the usual trappings of the royal court have been moved to make space for nearly a dozen long wooden tables, all arranged in rows leading up to the one raised table, perpendicular to the others, where the royal family–and Phainon–sits. The room’s usual cold stone and clear light have been replaced by the warmth of torchlight and dazzling chandeliers, the golden light bouncing off jewelry and copper mugs, diffusing through the haze of incense smoke. It seems to Phianon that the whole of Castrum Kremnos, unrestrained and boisterous in their joy, has gathered in the great hall, bedecked in their finest clothes and jewels. All to celebrate Mydei; and celebrate Mydei they do.

The party is magnificent. The food is bountiful and decadent, and there is drink enough to drown in. The entertainment is fast-paced and nearly nonstop. The hall is full of dances, wrestling matches, and all kinds of elaborate displays of strength and beauty. It’s impossible to pick what event to watch, but in all honesty, Phainon mostly watches Mydei. Phainon watches Mydei preen with pride as his somatophylakes perform an elaborately choreographed reenactment of ancient Kremnoan victories. He watches Mydei try not to squirm in his seat as his mother gives a speech about his accomplishments and virtues. He watches as Mydei smiles, broad and unrefined, as the somatophylakes sneak him another glass of wine.

“One more, for courage?” Hephaestion wheedles, pushing the goblet of pomegranate wine towards Mydei.

“You know you don’t have to sneak back here?” Phainon says with a laugh. “We can all just enjoy the wine normally.”

Hephaestion’s grin just widens, devious. “Absolutely not, this is far more fun,” he says, once again pestering Mydei to take the glass.

Mydei pushes him away, fond. “You know I’ve already had too much,” he says, hiccuping slightly, having already been subject to his fair share of wine. Hephaestion, too kind for his own good, takes the hint and turns his attention to Phainon.

“Well then, perhaps for the blushing bride?” he says, gesturing to Phainon with the overfull glass of wine.

“Oh, piss off,” Phainon says, but he takes the glass anyway, much to the delight of Hephaestion and the other somatophylakes. Since Phainon gained Mydei’s approval, the somatophylakes have warmed up to him considerably, and Phainon has gotten used to their teasing and crass jokes. He knows their jabs are signs of respect and a way of inclusion. It had been a strange adjustment, from the rigour of The Grove and the politicking of Okhema, but Phainon has found he appreciates the genuine openness shown by Mydei’s friends.

Suddenly, the background noise of the party doubles in volume as attendees start pushing the long tables back against the walls. The scratching of the wooden tables against stone floors and the cacophony of eager voices directing the movement almost drowns out the music, and Hephaestion has to lean in close to be heard.

“Hurry up,” Hephaestion says, eyes bright, “the dance is starting soon!”

“We’re dancing?” Phainon says, incredulous, “And you want me to drink more?”

“Yeah, you handle drink better than Mydei here,” Hephaestion says with a laugh. Then he suddenly turns serious. “Mydei told you about the dance, right?”

“Yes, I told him,” Mydei interrupts. “We’ve been practicing all week.” Mydei gets up from his chair, wobbling just enough for Phainon to notice. With this, Phainon realizes that everyone else has already moved to the open dance floor, and that only Hephaestion stays with them, the others scattered away to their positions.

“Oh, Prince Mydeimos,” Peucesta calls from the band, “won’t you join your countrymen in merriment? Tonight is in your honor!” The crowd erupts into cheers once more as the band plays an opening chord. Phainon, Mydei, and Hephaestion are truly the last ones out of place. Everyone else has either taken their place with the musicians or in one of the long lines of paired dancers. Even Gorgo and Eurypon have taken their spot at the front of the crowd; Gorgo enthusiastically waves the two of them over, and Eurypon looks almost pleased for once.

Mydei grumbles slightly at Pecusta’s tease and his mother’s excitement, and Phainon has to laugh. Mydei’s dislike of this party is so endearingly out of step with his typical confidence.

“We can’t hold everyone up, now can we,” Phainon jokes, downing his drink in one gulp as Hephaestion pulls them into the fray. They jostle their way through the crowd and stumble into place, right between Mydei’s parents and the somatophylakes.

Now that everyone is in place, the music grows louder and the tempo starts to increase as everyone begins to shout and clap in time with the song. Phainon stands face to face with Mydei, unable to stop smiling as he waits for the choreography to start. Mydei looks as flushed as Phainon feels and– Titans, red really is his color. He is so handsome it makes Phainon’s teeth ache. Never before has Phainon wanted something the way he wants to be close to Mydei. He doesn’t know exactly when it happened. During the spar, the kiss in the library, maybe some time during the quiet mornings in between. He doesn’t know when, but there’s no denying that Phainon has fully fallen for Mydei, and now he doesn’t know what to do with his emotions.

The music builds, the clapping has turned to stomping, it’s almost time to start.

“Ready?” Mydei asks, his smile crooked and free. He extends a hand to Phainon, offering himself as his partner in this dance. “But you might have to lead,” he adds with a giggle. A giggle! Mydei could kill him with that laugh.

image by Eos

“What do you mean,” Phainon hisses as he takes Mydei’s hand. “You can’t be that drunk!”

“Hephaestion and the others tried very hard,” Mydei says. “Don’t worry, we’ll be fine.” He giggles again, intent on sending Phainon to an early grave–he won’t make it another year at this rate. But before he can say anything, the music swells and everyone around them shouts as one, then Mydei snaps into position, pulling Phainon with him.

Kremnoan dances are nothing like the dances Phainon learned in Okhema. They are more like a pantomimed fight than anything he is familiar with. They are full of rhythmic stomping, dramatic spins and dips, a constant push and pull between the partners. This specific dance is meant to symbolize the founding of Castrum Kremnos, a ceremonial tribute to the royal family.

The dance starts with a whirlwind of spins. Partners hold hands and toss themselves left and right and left again. There is no true leader in these dances, but despite his earlier words Mydei still leads, pulling Phainon along after him like it’s natural.

They stay close throughout the dance, hands clasped together and leaning into each other’s gravity, and it feels good. It feels like it is the most natural thing in the world. It’s easy to get caught up in the joy of the music and everyone around them. It should be overwhelming, but it’s not. Their practice has paid off, and Phainon and Mydei complete the dance without any issues, falling into step without having to think.

When the song ends, Phainon tries to move away, but before he can take a single step, another song starts and Mydei pulls him back in.

“But I don’t know this one,” Phainon whines.

“That’s okay, it’s not hard,” Mydei says, easy as anything. He’s smiling ear to ear, hair mussed and eyes bright. This sort of celebration, these dances, are familiar to Mydei, and despite himself, he’s enjoying them. He wants Phainon to join him. He wants Phainon to share in this joy that makes up a part of his home. Phainon is helpless to refuse, and clumsily follows Mydei through the next set of steps.

Phainon is certain he gets almost all of them wrong. He tries to follow Mydei’s lead, but he keeps getting distracted by how lovely Mydei looks, by the warmth of his body and the strong flex of his muscles as they move. In the end, no one criticizes his bad dancing, and Mydei beams at him, looking irrationally proud.

After that, the celebration doesn’t stop. Mydei drags Phainon through the paces of two more partnered dances, and after most of the crowd has dissipated, the somatophylakes pull both of them into a large, boisterous circle dance which Phainon adores–even if he missed the change in direction twice and Mydei stepped on his feet. It is too free and exuberant not to enjoy. The music, the laughter, the smells of wine and burning candles, all of it makes the world feel diffused with the same sort of light that bursts through the clouds right after a storm: glorious and gorgeous.

They’re having so much fun they hardly notice when the party starts to wind down around them. Phainon referees a drinking competition between Ptolemy and Leonnius, he fetches pomegranate milk for Mydei, and even manages to tie him at arm wrestling. All the while, Phainon laughs easily and smiles wide. He lets his gaze linger on Mydei longer than is wise, but it can hardly be called indecent, can it? They are married, after all.

It’s only when Gorgo and Eurypon approach the group of friends that they realize how late it’s gotten. The queen tells them quietly, her own voice hoarse from laughter, that she and Eurypon are heading to bed, and they should consider doing so as well. Of course, the group protests any idea of ending festivities. We need to celebrate Mydei until morning comes, they say. And they make a solid effort, playing silly games and inventing horrible songs to sing for several more hours, until just the seven of them remain in the great hall. It’s long after midnight when they finally lapse into silence and stumble back to their rooms.

Once Phainon and Mydei arrive in their bedroom, they realize how tired they truly are, and they collapse into bed together after doing just the bare minimum to ensure they’re clean. Phainon deliberately does not wash the golden paint off his face.

They're both exhausted to the point where it’s hard to stay awake, but it’s a happy, content, sort of tired. The way you feel after a hard day’s work; like you’ve earned it. It loosens their limbs and lowers their inhibitions, and without truly meaning to, they find themselves heaped into one pile of gangly limbs, unwilling to be even mere inches apart. Phainon won't call it cuddling–not now. Not when that's not something they do. Not when the both of them have sobered up too much to throw such terms around without a second thought. But somehow, the reservations Phainon knows he should have just slide right off him. He’s just too happy, still buzzy and light from the party, and none of his usual doubts seem to stick.

For a moment, neither of them speak, they don’t need to. They fill the space between them with the soft rustle of fabric and quiet bursts of residual laughter. It feels comfortable and right. Phainon could fall asleep like this, head tucked beneath Mydei’s chin, pillowed on his chest and arms slug close over his waist. He almost does. Then Mydei moves, shuffles a bit beneath him, and starts running his hand up and down Phainon’s forearm. From the delicate bones of his wrist, up to his elbow, and back again, leaving goosebumps in his wake. It could easily be comforting, a gentle caress to lull Phainon even further asleep. But Mydei is strangely tense and hesitant in his movements, like he’s thinking something through, and this motion is just a consequence of his need to be moving while in focus.

“I think this was the first time I’ve truly enjoyed one of these parties,” Mydei says eventually. Phainon exhales, realizing how tense he’d been while waiting for Mydei to share what was on his mind.

“That’s good, right,” Phainon says into the hollow of Mydei’s throat.

“I mean, yeah, of course it’s a good thing. It was… A relief to finally feel like I was part of the celebration, instead of just, I don’t know.” Mydei’s hand balls into a fist atop Phainon’s. He never hides his emotions, but that doesn’t mean they’re all pleasant to talk about or easy to describe. “It usually feels like I’m somehow different, always stuck on the outside. Like I was to be celebrated and praised but never included. The somatophylakes tried, but… This time was different.” Mydei pushes at Phainon’s shoulder, coaxing him out of his hiding place and looking him in the eye. “You made it different, Phainon. I don’t think I would have enjoyed it without you.”

“Oh,” Phainon says, dumbly, feeling extremely exposed. His heart swoops into his stomach and the rest of his insides all but explode with light until he’s full of it. If the palace surgeons were to choose this moment to slice him open and pry apart his ribs, they’d find nothing but candlelight. Dozens, maybe hundreds of candles all burning for Mydei.

Phainon can’t speak, can hardly think; and he suddenly, irrationally, fears he might start crying. What is he supposed to say to that? Thank you feels laughably insufficient. But what else can he say that wouldn’t result in him offering up his entire heart and soul on a platter? Which maybe wouldn’t be so bad. Phainon has no reason to think that Mydei would be cruel; he’s even fairly sure Mydei wouldn’t reject him. It all just feels sudden, a confession like a sneak attack.

Mydei’s eyes narrow–he’s waiting for a response. “Thank you,” Phainon squeaks, unable to think of anything else in time. It feels as inadequate as he’d feared, but his heart’s moved to his throat and Mydei’s eyes are still narrow, still searching for something more. “I– I had a good time too, Mydei,” Phainon stutters out, frantic, unraveling. He really might cry. “I always enjoy spending time with you, Mydei, and I– I just. I don’t know how to talk about this without it sounding so pathetic or feeling like I’m going to throw up. Mydei–”

But then Mydei shoots up, suddenly serious, and Phainon’s mind skids to a halt, his reaction split in too many directions for any of them to stick.

“Oh,” is all Mydei says before coughing so violently his body shakes with the force of it. He coughs a second time, then a third, before he is able to straighten up. When Mydei wipes his mouth, Phainon realizes there is blood at the corners of his lips. His hand is covered in it.

“Fuck,” Phainon swears, already in a panic. Bile rises up his throat as he frantically tries to piece this together, but it feels like he’s been replaced with static. No longer a young man, just grating, sickly static in the shape of one.

“Mydei, what’s wrong,” Phainon asks, pleads really, as he fights with his own mind to stay present. It’s too easy to fall into the dark corners of his mind. They’re only parts of him left untouched by the static. Dark and miserable spirals that tell him this is his fault. This always happens when he gets too close. He can’t do this. Why can’t he do anything now, when it matters. All his training, all he’s already been through, and now is when he freezes? Stuck in place, clinging to Mydei as he coughs again and again, dripping blood down his chin, onto their bed.

The coughs slow and for a second, Phainon thinks that’s a good thing, but then Mydei’s breath goes labored and slow, and he sways, eyelids fluttering, seemingly spending an extraordinary amount of energy just to stay composed and upright. He turns to Phainon, one hand raised, as if to calm a startled animal. How kind Mydei is, Phainon thinks, distant. Even in visible distress, he still spares a moment to comfort Phianon.

“Phainon,” Mydei wheezes, “it’s not as bad as it looks.” His whole body heaves and blood pools at the corners of his mouth.

“It looks pretty bad,” Phainon says. “Should- Should I call a doctor.” Phainon notices, as if from afar, that the words coming out of his mouth sound halfway-reasonable. Which is strange, because he doesn’t register saying them, or even believe he’s the one who’s said them. Something must have possessed him, then, taken over his body as his mind is trapped in the static just beyond reality. Stuck watching Mydei suffer as he does nothing to help him.

Mydei waves him off, but his movements are getting sluggish. Phainon can’t understand why he seems so relaxed about this. “No need, I’ll come back pretty quick from this,” he says, then he groans, annoyed. “Someone must have slipped poison into one of my drinks.”

“Poison!” Phainon chokes out, his voice cracking in a way it hasn’t in years.

“Phainon, I’ll be fine,” Mydei says, serious, even as he starts to slur his words. “You’re forgetting this can’t kill me.”

With the last of his strength, Mydei wraps his hand around Phainon’s wrist, and Phainon realizes what is about to happen right before Mydei tells him, the understanding settling over him like ice water.

“I’m going to die, Phainion,” Mydei says, voice hardly above a whisper, “but stay here with me, please. We don’t know if the assassin is still in the palace, and I– I want you to be there when I come back.”

Mydei wheezes, then he rolls over and vomits off the side of the bed. Phainon can smell the bitterness of it from where he sits, and something about the smell shocks him back into his body. Finally, he feels real enough to move his body again, and he pulls Mydei up to lay properly on the bed, wiping his mouth with the edge of his chiton. Mydei’s hand fumbles weakly, trying to grab for something, and Phainon clasps it in both of his without a second thought.

“Why are you crying?” Mydei whispers, managing to scold Phainon even as his voice leaves him. Phainon doesn’t think he’s crying, but when he touches his face, his fingers come back wet. “I’ll be right back,” Mydei says, right before he goes slack in Phainon’s arms, eyes clouding over with death.

Chapter Summary

Time for the story to end. Mydeimos is alive and Phainon loves him. Confession comes easy after what they've been through. They can finally speak their feelings, and act on them too. In more... physical ways.

Chapter Notes

AND NOW WE FINALLY END!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Thank you so so so sososooo much for reading and enjoying this fic. There were many, many moments throughout writing this that i almost gave up on it, but i had such incredible support from my friends that i pushed through. AND ITS BEEN SO WORTH IT <333

SO ONCE AGAIN, THANK YOU TO EVERYONE WHO HAS HELPED MEEE. Thank you to Rea, Wax, Eos, Ghost, River, Aewin, Alan, and ALL the myphaideilings. cheers to me finally finishing this

The second worst seven minutes of Phainon’s life pass slowly and in a strange haze. The world goes dark around the edges as he holds Mydei’s limp body–dead body–and waits for him to come back to life. Just like he’d asked. He tries to remind himself that Mydei will come back. You’re forgetting this can’t kill me; those had been his exact words. Phainon knows this. He knows this; he trusts Mydei with everything he has. Phainon knows that Mydei is telling the truth, that he’ll come back. But that doesn’t change the fact that currently, Mydei is unmistakably dead. Mydei is dead, in the bed they share, before Phainon got to kiss him for a second time. His body is cold and lifeless, blood and bile pooling at the corners of his mouth, reminding Phainon that for all that this moment may look peaceful, Mydei was wracked with pain in the moments leading up to his death.

As he sits and waits, a festering and despicable corner of his brain squirms to life, whispering all the anxious lies Phainon thought he’d outgrown. Staticky and cruel, this part of Phainon reminds him that this is his fault. Mydei will die in truth and it will be his fault. Everyone he’s ever loved has died. He half convinces himself to leave. To deny his feelings and run away from Castrum Kremnos. To find a way to orchestrate his death out in the countryside, somehow make it clear it was an accident so he doesn’t void the treaty. Maybe he has to write a will before he leaves. Something to keep Mydei safe, to keep their kingdoms safe. To do the job he was supposed to.

Alone and to himself, in this terrible moment of pretending that he no longer exists, Phainon can admit that he loves Mydei. The confession of a dead man means nothing.

Then, there is movement–Mydei is alive again. With a violent shake and a breath that sounds more like a death rattle than a revival, Mydei is back, shivering in Phainon’s arms like he never left.

“Mydei,” Phainon gasps. It’s hard to speak through the tears and his still stinging throat, but he does his best before collapsing around Mydei, enveloping him in a haphazard and overwhelmed embrace.

“Phainon,” Mydei replies, voice still sticky and rough with the stiffness of death. “You’re still here.”

Phainon opens his mouth to respond but finds he can’t, he’s crying too much to speak.

“Phainon,” Mydei says, fond, exasperated, fighting back the tightness in his own voice. It strikes Phainon then, how much he loves hearing Mydei say his name. He no longer calls him Deliverer, now using his name instead. Phainon. Mydei says his name like the man it belongs to is worth cherishing. Like he loves him. Does Mydei love him? Is that something Phainon can hope for when he himself is still unsure how to actualize love without catastrophe?

“You cry too much,” Mydei scolds. He isn’t mad; he’s crying himself now.

“You’re worth crying over,” Phainon says. The vulnerability comes easy now. He wonders if it will stay like that. He hopes so. “And of course I stayed,” he insists. “I don’t think I could have left if I wanted to.”

Mydei does not reply, but he smiles, eyes bright despite the tears, then pulls Phainon in to properly hold him. They lay together on the bed, entwined close enough to convince Phainon that Mydei truly has survived. Phainon wishes they could stay like this for the rest of the night, safe together; but even if the adrenaline would let them sleep, Mydei insists they need to report the assassination attempt to his parents and the palace staff.

“You can stay and sleep,” Mydei offers from the bathroom as he cleans the blood from his face. Phainon grumbles from the bed, but despite his grogginess, he swings himself up to his feet.

“No, I won’t be able to sleep anyway,” Phainon says. He walks towards Mydei, watches over his shoulder as he dries his face. “And I don’t want to leave you alone… I don’t want to be alone,” he adds quietly. The idea of being away from Mydei is almost unbearable. Just the few minutes Mydei had spent cleaning up were almost too much. As soon as Mydei left their bed, Phainon started to feel sick and itchy. Even now, standing only a few paces away, Phainon still feels uneasy, like anything short of plastering himself to Mydei’s side leaves the possibility for danger to slip in.

“Alright,” Mydei says, turning to face Phainon. “We’ll go together.” He offers a hand to Phainon.

Phainon looks down at the offered hand for a moment. Despite his clinginess and anxiety, he is still unsure how to act on those emotions. He might cry again. Mydei is too kind.

Phainon takes Mydei’s hand. He laces their fingers together and steps in close. Mydei is warm beside him. Alive.

Phainon laughs, self-deprecating, and says, “you’re the one who just died, and here you are, comforting me.”

“Your foolishness never ceases to amaze me,” Mydei says, voice incongruously soft. “Being close to you is a comfort to me as well.”

Phainon stares at him, a lump in his throat and candlelight in his veins. Mydei offers his affection and his love so freely. Phainon hopes one day to be worthy of it.

“Okay,” Phainon replies, quiet. “Thank you.”

Mydei shakes his head. There is no need to voice the rebuttal. Phainon knows he does not need to thank Mydei for his kindness, but he is so grateful for it that he feels he must. He is so wildly, fantastically grateful to have Mydei in his life. It is only right to let him know.

It turns out Castorice had been right, Phainon thinks, smiling to himself, the Crown Prince did end up surprising him.

***

The walk to the guardroom is uneventful. There are no nefarious assassins hiding in the shadows or panicked chaos in the halls, but when they arrive, Krateros is already there, disheveled and irritated.

“Oh, Prince Mydeimos,” he says, surprised, as Phainon and Mydei walk in. “I was just about to send for you.”

It’s not only Krateros, in addition to the regular guards, nearly all of the guard captains and even two military generals are all packed into the small command room. Perhaps the chaos they had feared would be in the castle was all stuffed into this one room. Phainon hopes the assassination attempt was not part of a larger threat.

“Krateros, you needed me?” Mydei asks, concerned. He’s noticed the unusual crowd as well. “I suspect we may have the same thing to discuss.” Mydei pauses, waits for a nod from Krateros before continuing. “Earlier this evening I was the victim of an assassination attempt by poison.” The room erupts in surprised gasps and exclamations of fury. “I have recovered now, and Phainon stayed by my side until I revived. However we have not identified the assailant, and it is possible they are still within the castle.”

“I see,” Krateros replies. “We indeed had the same news to discuss. Just half an hour ago, an intruder was apprehended during a routine patrol. We took him to a holding cell before sending for you. He seemed fairly nonthreatening, with no weapons, and his speech was largely incoherent.” Krateros takes a steadying breath, fists clenched at his sides. “My Prince, I greatly regret that this enemy had the chance to harm you before we found him. Trust this oversight will be remedied.”

“It is not your fault,” Mydei says. “However, I am worried he might have an accomplice, or maybe more than one.”

“We’ve searched the castle and found no one else,” a guard captain says from behind Krateros. “But we will do another full sweep just to be sure.”

“Good. Hopefully this man was acting alone,” Mydei says. “At the end of the day, it is good he went after me, as opposed to anyone else. It seems the attacker had incorrect information about my mortality.”

Everyone present cheers, rallied by Mydei’s survival. He has once again proven his strength and immortality. Mydei looks perfectly at home here, surrounded by warriors and his countrymen. He will be a glorious king one day. One would be a fool not to follow him. The victorious energy in the room is impossible to ignore. Even exhausted and so recently revived, Mydei smiles and raises a fist in proud salute.

Throughout all of this, he does not let go of Phainon’s hand. It makes Phainon so giddy he has trouble focusing on the tactical discussion between Mydei and Krateros. As soon as he learns that the assassin has been apprehended and most likely acted alone, Phainon feels his adrenaline finally crash. He leans against Mydei, uncaring that they are in a room of Kremnoan guards and soldiers. It is the middle of the night and he just watched his husband die, so at least for now, Phainon will allow himself this indulgence.

The conversation fades to pleasant background noise as Phainon fights to stay awake. He has no idea how Mydei is so coherent. Maybe being revived gives him extra energy? He’ll have to ask. Then suddenly, the door bursts open and Eurypon and Gorgo rush in.

“Krateros, I’m sorry we’re late,” Eurypon says. He gives a cursory nod to all present before continuing. “Lead me to the holding cell and explain the situation on the way. I will ensure this assassin receives the maximum punishment possible.” He does not speak to Mydei, only sparring his son a single, tight glance of relief.

He is angry, Phainon realizes. It is hard to tell, given how serious and tense Eurypon is at all times, but there is real hatred in his expression now. If Phainon were more awake, or perhaps if he had seen this expression in his first weeks in Castrum Kremnos, he would be terrified.

Eurypon and Krateros storm out of the room, followed by a group of high ranking guards. The room seems to open up as he leaves, the air itself feeling lighter.

“Mydeimos, Phainon,” Queen Gorgo says, rushing over to the two of them. She wraps both of them in a hug, squeezing tightly before pulling back. She keeps her hands on their shoulders but her expression is steely, utterly serious. “What happened?” The hug sends Phainon reeling. He had not considered Queen Gorgo might care about him along with her son.

“Mother. I’m alright, and Krateros has everything under control,” Mydei says.

“That is not what I asked, Mydeimos. What happened?” Gorgo’s voice is stern, but there is unmistakable warmth in her face and posture. There is a softness to Gorgo that Mydei naturally reflects. Face to face like this, it is clear just how similar they are.

Mydei tenses briefly and squeezes Phainon’s hand. A part of him is uncomfortable at the prospect of discussing the assassination attempt with his mother. But he steadies quickly. He explains the assassination attempt, gives details when his mother asks, and manages to stay calm and professional. Despite his clinical speech, hearing the details of the night upsets Phianon more than he had expected. When Gorgo turns to him and asks if he has anything else to add, his voice is thin and rough. At least he has nothing to add, Mydei explained everything perfectly.

Gorgo sits in thought for a moment after Mydei’s explanation. “I know there is probably nothing we can learn, but it might be useful if you went to see a doctor,” she says. “Maybe they could find clues to what poison was used, make sure there are no lingering effects.”

“I’m perfectly fine, Mother,” Mydei insists. “And we know they won’t find anything.”

“Still, it would give some peace of mind,” Gorgo replies, a slight frown on her face. Phainon realizes, miserably, that if Mydei has to go to the medical clinic, he probably cannot stay glued to his side.

“I will go in the morning,” Mydei says firmly. “I am confident that I will be safe and healthy until then.”

“Mydeimos–”

“–I want to spend the rest of the night in my room, comfortable and with my husband,” Mydei interrupts, pleading. Phainon snaps his head towards Mydei, thrilled–if a little embarrassed–that Mydei would claim him in public like that. “Mother. I will be fine,” Mydei continues, softer. “I am confident that Krateros and the guards will ensure there are no accomplices, and if there are, I am confident that Phainon and I can handle them… Please.”

Gorgo sighs, hands on her hips. She looks at Mydei with an expression of fond exasperation that Phainon recognizes from Aglaea’s conversations with Cipher–and from the memories of his own mother, all those years ago.

“I can’t convince you, can I,” Gorgo says. “Alright, have it your way. But I expect to see you in the clinic tomorrow, understand?"

“Yes, Mother,” Mydei replies, clearly relieved. He turns to Krateros. “Sir, do you need anything else from us?”

“No, we have it covered. I’ll send for you if the situation changes.”

Mydei gives a slight bow to Krateros and leans over to give his mother a quick kiss on the cheek. Then, formalities over, he all but runs out of the guard room, speeding back to his room and dragging Phainon behind him.

***

They wake up late. Midmorning light filters in through the curtains and the soft smell of dew already gives way to the sweetness of warm dirt. There are not many opportunities for the two of them to linger in bed like this. Phainon’s schedule is looser, but most days see Mydei up and busy right after sunrise. A special exception had been made for today. Most of the palace is recovering from the festivities the night before, and Phainon suspects the assassination attempt has earned them more grace than was already afforded.

When Phainon opens his eyes, Mydei is already awake, lying on his side, head pillowed on his hand. The look on his face is so incomprehensibly tender that Phainon squeezes his eyes shut on instinct.

“Don’t hide,” Mydei says with a small laugh. His voice is still rough from sleep. Those eyes, this voice–Phainon thinks he might die. “You’re obviously awake.” He pokes Phainon in the cheek, teasing him into opening his eyes again.

“Nope, not awake,” Phainon squeaks, burying his face in their pillows. It’s a ridiculous claim. So far from the truth it can’t even be called a lie. Phainon can’t keep it up. The absurdity of his own words forces a laugh from him and he opens his eyes despite himself.

“That was quick,” Mydei says, smiling. His smile. His eyes crease, his face dimples, his posture relaxes. Phainon wants to see that smile every single morning.

“I can only be so ridiculous,” Phainon replies.

“Yeah, we’ll see about that,” Mydei teases.

They exhale at the same time, a laugh on their breath, then a beat passes and they are frozen in the moment. They stare at each other. It is one part simple appreciation–it is hard to have such a handsome man in your bed and not want to stare at him–but it is another part reassurance. The longer they look at each other, the more they can convince themselves that this is real. They survived the night.

“Good morning,” Phainon says quietly, breaking the silence. He is certain he will combust if he keeps staring at Mydei. Combust or do something exponentially more dangerous.

“Morning,” Mydei says, brushing an unruly strand of hair from Phainon’s forehead.

“I’m sure my bedhead is atrocious.”

“Yeah, it always is.”

They both laugh and press forehead to forehead, eagerly falling into the gravity between them.

Phainon tries to ignore it, he really does. He wants to laugh with Mydei and languish in the gentle closeness they’ve found themselves in, but the scratching sensation behind his sternum refuses to dissipate and his pulse quickens more each minute he ignores it.

“Mydei,” Phainon interrupts, voice suddenly no more than a whisper. “Is everything really alright? Are you okay?”

Mydei’s eyebrows furrow and he looks pained for a second. Then he takes Phainon’s hand and presses it to his chest, warm, and bare from sleep. He holds Phainon’s hand in place until Phianon calms enough to focus on the body beneath his palm.

“Feel my heartbeat,” Mydei says, just stern enough that Phainon has no choice but to listen. He closes his eyes and focuses his attention. Sure enough, after a moment, he can feel the soft ba-dum ba-dum of Mydei’s heart.

“I can feel it,” he murmurs, entranced.

“That is proof I’m alive, Phainon,” Mydei says softly, his voice lowered to Phainon’s volume. “Dying is never pleasant, but among my deaths, last night’s was far from the worst.”

“But you died,” Phainon insists.

“Can it truly be called a death if I am here with you now?” Mydei asks, pressing his weight into Phianon’s palm. He is intense, all fire and passion and life. It is irrefutable. Not even the most cunning of Phainon’s anxieties can deny it. “Here, I have something to show you,”

Mydei sits up, gently pulling Phainon along with him. As they move, the blankets slip down with a quiet hiss and pool at their laps, letting the first warm breeze of afternoon blow across their shoulders. Mydei leans forward, arching his back into the curve of a bow.

“My back. The tenth vertebra,” he says, his voice strangely distant as Phainon stares at the expanse of Mydei’s back–tries not to get distracted by the way his muscles flex and pull with every breath. “That is my weak spot. I will not die unless I am struck through the tenth thoracic vertebra.”

Phainon’s heart jumps in his chest. He has been handed a gift, something to cherish and protect for the rest of his days. He reaches out; pulls back. Suddenly, touching Mydei’s back feels too intimate. His fingers hover just out of reach, shaking.

“You can touch,” Mydei says. The words have a weight that reminds Phainon of the first time he held a sword. Mydei lets the invitation settle between them and waits for Phainon to find his courage.

The entirety of Phainon’s life seems to rush past him in reverse as he reaches out to touch Mydei. It’s such a small movement, but with it comes the sanctity of something preordained. Phainon is suddenly sure that every moment of his life–of all his past lives and future reincarnations–has led him here.

Phainon’s fingers reach the base of Mydei’s neck, and he shivers at the touch. From there he drifts down and counts each ridge of Mydei’s spine. One, two, three…

“There,” Mydei says when Phainon reaches ten.

Phainon’s body is buzzing as he lays his hand flat over Mydei’s weak spot. “This is it?” He asks.

“Yes, that’s it,” Mydei says. He is so quiet, so still, his back perfectly on display. “Attack there and I’d be dead. Unable to come back.”

Phainon whimpers and lilts forward, pressing his face to Mydei’s back, leaning his weight against it. The idea of Mydei’s death, even hypothetical, is too miserable to bear. The feeling opens up like a cavern inside of him, a great darkness that shatters his heart and pulls his breath into its depth. It is incomprehensible.

“How many people know?” Phainon asks, voice rough.

“You are the fourth,” Mydei replies. “My parents, Hephaestion, and now you.”

“I will protect this secret with my life,” Phainon says, placing a kiss against the weak spot to hide the way his voice breaks. “As long as I live, I will protect your back. I swear it, Mydeimos.”

Mydei gasps, and Phainon feels his skin burst into goosebumps beneath his lips. Then Mydei reaches behind him and pulls Phainon up by the arm. It forces his shoulder into an odd angle, and he has to fumble a bit to get Phainon where he wants him, but he is so surefire, confident and quick, that no awkwardness registers. As is so often the case, Mydei chose a vision of the future and set an inexorable path towards its creation. When Mydei climbs upon his lap and holds his face in both his hands, Phainon feels as if he was always meant to be there.

“Phainon of Aedes Elysiae, I swear to you,” Mydei says, breathing fast, forehead pressed to Phainon’s, “as long as I live, I will fight to protect you as well, body and soul.”

Mydei looks like he might say more, but Phanion can’t stop the words from bubbling up inside of him. “I love you,” he gasps. For the first time since his family died, since Aedes Elysiae burned, he knows this love is true and strong, and it cannot hurt him.

Mydei surges forward and kisses him. He tangles his fingers in Phainon’s hair and pulls him close, slotting their mouths together. Phainon goes weightless. With the sparkling pop of a bubble surrendering to the air, Phainon explodes into shimmering lightness. Held together by Mydei’s touch alone, grounded only at the places their bodies meet.

Their lips slide together, wet and hot and alive. Mydei holds Phainon close, his kisses harsh and unrelenting. It is not unlike how he fights: demanding and unflinching in his strength. Challenging. The way a sculptor approaches a block of marble, or a whetstone meets a sword, Mydei uses his strength to coax the same from Phainon. Anything less would be an insult to them both. The realization rouses Phainon from his shocked bliss. He would be content to let Mydei devour him alive, but that is not what Mydei is asking of him.

It’s overwhelming, being encouraged in this way; to know Mydei is his to freely touch. Phainon scrambles for somewhere to put his hands, but it feels wrong to settle in any one place. He skates his hands down Mydei’s sides, up his back and across his strong shoulders and arms. He even dares to hold the weight of his chest. Mydei shivers when Phainon rolls a thumb over a nipple, and Phainon is awestruck. There is still so much to learn about Mydei, so many more reactions to catalog. At last, Phainon lets his hands come to rest at Mydei’s waist, fingers brushing over the exquisite cut of his hip before squeezing and pulling Mydei even closer.

When they part, they are both breathless.

“You love me,” Mydei repeats, wondrous and bright.

“I love you,” Phainon confirms.

Mydei laughs, the sound worthy of poems and epic ballads, and pulls Phainon into a hug. “I love you too,” he says into Phainon’s hair.

“Mydei,” Phainon begs, looping his arms around Mydei’s waist, “kiss me again.”

Mydei pulls back, just enough for Phainon to tilt his head up and meet his gaze. It feels right, to look up at him like this, to be a supplicant begging for Mydei’s favor. Mydei smiles, a blush already staining his proud cheeks, then with a tilt of the head and slight widening of the eyes, he grants Phainon what he desires.

It’s their fourth kiss. Third? Phainon is starting to think the number doesn’t matter anymore. Each kiss is more indulgent, intimate, and luxurious than the last. Mydei is a natural at it. His hands are everywhere, and he does wicked things with his tongue that leave Phainon dizzy. It forces a moan out of him, a sound Phainon has never heard himself make, and Mydei takes the opportunity to run his tongue across the roof of his mouth and the points of his teeth. He moans again and understanding falls into place. This is about reaching out to Mydei, asking to be as close as possible, and Mydei saying yes. It’s more than the relief of survival or the catharsis of confession. It is love–Phainon is certain that everything he does for the rest of his life will be about his love for Mydei–but more than that, it is the understanding that they are two halves of the same being, and this physicality is the closest they can get to remedy their separation.

“More,” Phainon breathes into the sliver of space between them. Mydei’s answering smile presses against his lips, beckoning, but before Phainon can kiss him again, Mydei rolls his hips; and suddenly, Phainon is blindingly aware of his arousal. He’s been mostly hard since Mydei climbed into his lap, but what had previously been a pleasant background hum is now a blisteringly hot fire, overpowering everything else. His hands drop to Mydei’s ass, almost on instinct, pulling him into another grind. Even through their undergarments, the press of Mydei’s arousal against his own is better than anything he’s felt in his life.

“Fuck, Mydei,” Phainon swears. He’s fully hard now, body electric with pleasure.
